text: Mark Twain's The Adventures of Tom Sawyer was excluded from the children's room of the Public Library in Brooklyn, N.Y., in 1876, and also from the Denver Public Library. In 1885 it was barred from the Concord, Massachusetts library as "trash and suitable only for the slums". It was later challenged in Richardson's high schools over "inappropriate language" and text that some might find "sensitive or controversial"; an alternate book was allowed.
